paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu, accompanied by Torii Shintaro, walked straight to the place of honor and seated himself beside Hideyori. Before greeting Hideyori, he leisurely surveyed the people who had gathered in the great audience hall.

paragraphs.source_en: It had become customary for every daimyo with an annual stipend of ten thousand koku or more to assemble here for the Festival of the Double Ninth. Yet now, nearly all the daimyo were away from Osaka. Apart from Asano Nagamasa and Mashita Nagamori in the foremost seats, everyone present was one of Hideyori's close retainers.

paragraphs.source_en: Mashita Nagamori and Natsuka Masaie had been driven into a dead end; their calculations had utterly failed. They had meant to draw the Asano and Maeda factions away from Ieyasu, only to find themselves mired in hatred and suspicion. Mitsunari must surely be cursing them for needlessly bringing Ieyasu into Osaka Castle. Worse still, those around Hideyori must already have come to regard the two men as traitors.
